template: Text someone you like but haven’t talked to in over a month and ask how they’ve really been, not just “wyd.”
Invite [person] to grab coffee, boba, or tea this week and offer two possible days or times.
Call a friend instead of texting and stay on the phone for at least 10 minutes.
Send a voice note to [person] telling them one thing you genuinely appreciate about them.
Ask a coworker, neighbor, or classmate if they want to grab lunch or a quick snack after work or class.
Invite [person] to do a walk-and-talk hang in your neighborhood, park, or downtown area for at least 30 minutes.
Choose one online friend or supporter and ask if they’d ever want to do a 20–30 minute video call to connect more.
Send a genuine, specific compliment to 3 people you already know, about their work, personality, or growth.
Ask [person] if they want to cowork or study together for an hour at a café, library, or your place.
Host a tiny hang: invite at least 1 person over for a low-pressure chill night such as game, movie, or music.
Ask a friend if they want to hit a grocery store or Target run together and treat it like a mini hang, not just an errand.
Invite [person] to watch a game, stream, or show together, either in person or via call with synced start time.
Ask a friend if they want to try a new restaurant, café, or food spot with you this week and actually set a time.
Reply to 5 people’s stories or posts today with something more meaningful than an emoji.
Ask [person] a deeper question than usual such as “What’s been on your mind lately?” and really listen.
Join a local meetup, class, or event where you don’t know anyone and introduce yourself to at least 2 people.
Ask someone you already know casually if they’d like to hang out one-on-one for the first time.
Send a long appreciation text to [person] explaining how they’ve impacted your life positively.
Ask a friend if they want to start a tiny ritual with you such as weekly walks, calls, or gym sessions.
Invite [person] to bring a friend and meet you somewhere public, letting your circles overlap a little.
Ask a coworker or classmate you like how they’re finding the job or class and share your honest take too.
Invite [person] to come with you to an event you’re already going to such as a show, open mic, or meetup.
Organize a tiny group hang of 3–5 people at a bar, café, park, or someone’s living room.
Ask a friend from your past neighborhood or school to catch up on a call or in person for at least 20 minutes.
Invite [person] to join you for a gym session, walk, or physical activity and actually show up on time.
Ask a friend what they’re excited about right now in life and ask at least one follow-up question.
Host a low-budget game night using whatever games or card decks you already have and invite at least 2 people.
Send [person] a link to a song, video, or meme that genuinely made you think of them and say why.
Ask someone in your life what they’re struggling with lately and just listen without giving advice unless they ask.
Invite [person] to run an errand with you such as shopping, picking something up, or dropping something off.
Join a recurring local thing such as a weekly class, meetup, or group and actually show up one time.
Ask a friend if they want to do a joint “work session” at your place, their place, or a café for 60–90 minutes.
Tell [person] directly that you enjoy their company and want to hang out more often.
Ask someone new at work, gym, or class how long they’ve been coming there and what they like about it.
Invite [person] to try a hobby you already like such as music, art, gaming, or gym and show them the basics.
Ask a friend if they want to plan a micro-trip such as a day trip to a nearby town or park in the next month.
Send a sincere apology to [person] if there’s someone you feel you lowkey dropped, ghosted, or offended in the past.
Ask someone you respect if they want to grab coffee so you can hear more about their story or path.
Invite [person] to a park hang: one blanket, some snacks, drinks, and at least 45 minutes of conversation.
Ask someone you already see regularly such as a barista, receptionist, or neighbor what their name is and remember it.
Send 3 check-in texts today that are more than “wyd” and ask something specific about their life.
Invite [person] to a “no phones” meal or coffee where both of you keep phones off the table the whole time.
Ask a friend if they want help with something specific such as moving, a project, or a creative idea and actually show up.
Ask [person] what they’ve been proud of lately and reflect it back to them verbally in your own words.
Invite a small group of 3–4 people to a low-key “bring your own snack” hang at a park or someone’s home.
Ask a friend from another city if they’d ever want to visit you and what they’d want to see in your area.
Send [person] an old photo or screenshot that reminds you of a good memory and talk about it for a bit.
Join a group activity where you have to talk to others such as a class, run club, game night, or meetup, and introduce yourself out loud.
Ask someone you like hanging out with if they know anyone they think you’d vibe with, and be open to an introduction.
Invite [person] to an early morning walk, coffee, or gym session before noon, then actually show up.
Ask a friend if they want to start a monthly ritual such as brunch, movie night, or creative session and schedule the first one.
Offer to help [person] with something small such as giving feedback on a project, reading something, or listening to a vent.
Ask a friend their opinion on something that actually matters to you such as a decision, outfit, or plan and thank them for being honest.
Invite [person] to do a “no money” hang like a walk, park sit, or library visit to prove you don’t need to spend to socialize.
Text 3 people the same question: “What’s something good that happened to you this week?” and respond to each answer properly.
Ask [person] if they’d like to collaborate with you on something small such as content, a creative idea, or a side project.
Choose one friend whose work or art you like and promote them once publicly such as sharing their link or story.
Invite [person] to explore a part of town neither of you go to often and walk one full block or area together.
Ask a friend from a different background than you about part of their upbringing or culture and listen without centering yourself.
Invite [person] to attend a class, workshop, or meetup with you and actually go, even if you feel awkward at first.
Ask someone online who supports your work or content if they’d like to hop on a quick 10–15 minute call sometime to say thanks.
Tell [person] about something you’re struggling with and let them respond instead of pretending everything is always fine.
Ask a friend what they want more of in their social life this year and ask how you can support that.
Invite [person] to a chill at-home night such as cooking together, takeout plus movie, or shared music session.
Ask someone you see regularly at the gym, café, or bus stop one extra question that moves the conversation past small talk.
Invite [person] to help you with something small such as giving feedback or trying a prototype, and make it clear there’s no pressure.
Send 5 quick check-in messages to people in different parts of your life such as work, school, hometown, and online.
Ask [person] if they want to join you in a mini challenge such as a week of walks, a reading challenge, or daily check-ins.
Tell someone, out loud, that you’re glad they’re in your life and watch their reaction without deflecting.
Invite [person] to come sit with you somewhere scenic such as a river, rooftop, or hill for at least 30 minutes of talking.
Ask a friend if there’s a show, movie, or game they want to share with you and let them pick for one night.
Invite [person] to “run an outside mission” with you such as a Walmart run, mall browse, or late-night snack trip.
Ask someone in your life what kind of friend they want to be better at being and share your own answer too.
Invite [person] to meet you halfway between both of your places for a neutral spot hang.
Ask a friend from a long time ago what they remember most about the time you spent together back then.
Invite [person] to a new spot you’ve never tried such as a café, bar, park, or late-night food place.
Ask someone at an event or meetup what made them decide to show up tonight and share your reason too.
Invite [person] to bring one of their friends you don’t know and meet all together for a chill hang.
Ask a friend what they want their life to look like in 5 years and ask at least two follow-up questions.
Invite [person] to a “focused work + chill after” hang where you both work for an hour then hang for at least 20 minutes.
Tell someone they can call or text you anytime about something specific such as breakups, creative blocks, or job stress—and mean it.
Invite [person] to a “bring your own drink” balcony, porch, or parking-lot conversation for at least 30 minutes.
Ask a friend what they feel they can’t really talk to most people about and see if they want to share.
Invite [person] to attend a live event with you such as a show, open mic, sports game, or local performance.
Ask someone whose hustle or creativity you respect if they’d be down to swap notes over coffee or a call.
Invite [person] to do a late-night drive or public transport ride with you to just talk and look at the city.
Ask a friend if you can vent about something for 5 minutes and then ask them if they want to vent about anything too.
Invite [person] to a grocery-store or market mission where the goal is to find one new snack or drink to try together.
Ask someone what friendship means to them and share one thing you wish more people knew about how to be your friend.
Invite [person] to a “phones away for 20 minutes” conversation where you both put your phones face down and just talk.
Ask a friend what they think your strengths are as a person and let them talk without arguing against it.
Invite [person] to join you in trying a new low-stakes hobby together such as sketching at a café, journaling, or photography walk.
Ask someone what they wish their social life looked like and listen fully before relating it back to yourself.
Invite [person] to a “creative night” where you both work on something such as music, drawing, writing, or planning, even if it’s rough.
Ask a friend what they remember about the first time they met you and share what you remember about them.
Invite [person] to go for a long walk or drive where you both take turns choosing topics to talk about.
Ask someone you trust to be honest about one thing you could do better as a friend and thank them for being real.
Invite [person] to a small, intentional hang where you each share one goal for the next month and how you can support each other.
Take the lead on planning one social thing this month, even if it’s tiny, instead of waiting for someone else to plan.
Choose 3 people you want in your long-term life and reach out to all 3 this week in a way that feels real, not surface-level.
